summary: Independent re-verification of the 2-gap ticket (self-bug tool_error detection + project brain memory finding). All 11 new dedicated tests pass, full targeted regression suite passes (157/157), 5 pre-existing out-of-scope failures reproduce with the same signatures as pre-fix baseline, live-pipeline direct-DB repro fires new tool_error rows with correct sources for BOTH incidents (internal_directive_guard + handoff_diff_safety_guard), Part A regression via /chat/send (exec_usage/injection_scanner prompt) returns cleanly with leak_stripped=true and no leaked directive text, dead_end_leak sibling category unaffected, Part B live HTTP repro confirms brain updated_at is UNCHANGED after a no-keyword-match turn and correctly bumps + adds redis/django tech_stack + new decision row after a decision-phrase turn on p_r10_testbed_e2e, benign /chat/send turn creates ZERO false-positive tool_error entries. Documented pre-existing asymmetry (turn.py has no update_brain_from_conversation call) grep-confirmed.

minor.issue: RuntimeWarning 'coroutine emit was never awaited' when apply_output_guards is called with no running loop (expected fallback branch), cosmetic only — test_no_running_loop_never_raises still passes and the guard's rewrite return value is unaffected

critical_code_review_comments: Fire-and-forget self_bug.emit() wiring in apply_output_guards() is correctly wrapped in try/except and swallows RuntimeError when no event loop is running — preserves the 'never break the real turn' contract.
_SOURCE_CAUSES precise mapping preserves self_bug.py's 'no-invented-cause' discipline (unrelated sources fall back to generic tool_error cause).

Documented (out-of-scope) asymmetry: routers/chat/turn.py (/chat/send) reads brain context but never writes; frontend uses /chat/stream so not the live user path — grep-confirmed unchanged this round. Worth revisiting in a follow-up if any non-frontend caller ever uses /chat/send.

Narrow keyword/decision-phrase gate in update_brain_from_conversation is by design (lightweight, no LLM) — a QA-heavy conversation history may never trigger it. Consider a low-cost follow-up: capture rough per-project 'no-write turns count' so the admin panel can distinguish 'no brain data because conversation didn't match triggers' from 'no brain data because wiring is broken' without needing to grep code.

rca of the issue: Gap 1: apply_output_guards() had two most-recent guards (strip_leaked_tool_directives, strip_stray_code_blocks_near_handoff) that actively rewrote content but never invoked self_bug.emit('tool_error', ...) — nothing anywhere else emitted tool_error either. Fix added a fire-and-forget _fire_self_bug() call immediately after each guard actually mutates content, threading session_id/user_id kwargs from both real call sites (turn.py, stream.py). Precise per-source cause text added to services/self_bug.py's new _SOURCE_CAUSES dict. Verified live: 2 new rows appear with correct source/session/confidence/severity, benign turns create no rows. Gap 2: not a bug — read/write both key on the same plain-string project_id in the same project_brains collection (confirmed via grep and 2 live turns); update_brain_from_conversation only persists on ~28 hardcoded tech/decision keyword patterns, so a mostly-debugging conversation history genuinely never trips it. Live re-verified: a no-keyword-match /chat/stream turn left updated_at completely unchanged (2026-09-14T04:19:44.901000), a decision-phrase turn bumped it to 2026-09-14T04:42:44.206000 and added redis/django to tech_stack plus a new decisions row. Reported as working-as-designed per ticket instruction.
